name: Early-onset Progressive Neurodegeneration-Blindness-Ataxia-Spasticity Syndrome
aliases: Early-onset Neurodegeneration with Visual Impairment and Motor Dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Early-onset Progressive Neurodegeneration-Blindness-Ataxia-Spasticity Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive neurodegenerative course with onset in infancy or early childhood
Bilateral severe visual impairment or blindness developing within first decade
Combination of cerebellar ataxia and pyramidal spasticity causing motor dysfunction
Identification of pathogenic variant in associated gene (if known)
Exclusion of other neurodegenerative or metabolic disorders by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: progressive neurodegeneration, early-onset blindness, and combined ataxia with spasticity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended but not mandatory for diagnosis; clinical presentation is key.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive bilateral optic atrophy leading to blindness
pathognomonic.notes: Typically develops within first 5 years of life
searchTerms: gradual loss of both optic nerves
progressive blindness from optic nerve damage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early-onset cerebellar ataxia with gait instability
pathognomonic.notes: Progresses over time causing severe motor impairment
Leads to increased muscle tone and hyperreflexia

common.notes: Speech impairment due to motor dysfunction

searchTerms: weak upper arm and thigh muscles

common.notes: Often present early in disease course

occasional.symptomName: Scoliosis secondary to spasticity and muscle imbalance
Feeding difficulties and failure to thrive

rare.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to bulbar involvement
rare.notes: May require ventilatory support in advanced stages
searchTerms: respiratory failure due to bulbar muscles
difficulty breathing from throat muscle involvement

rare.notes: Severe seizure episodes in minority of patients

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; metabolic screening typically negative
CSF analysis may show mild protein elevation
imaging: MRI brain showing cerebellar atrophy and optic nerve thinning
Spinal cord MRI may show corticospinal tract degeneration
other: Electrophysiological studies showing delayed visual evoked potentials
Nerve conduction studies consistent with mild peripheral neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated optic neuropathy without prominent ataxia or spasticity

redFlags: Rapidly progressive vision loss in early childhood
Combination of ataxia and spasticity with developmental regression
Presence of seizures or respiratory insufficiency in a young child
references: Recent Advances in Pediatric Neurodegenerative Disorders, Journal of Child Neurology, 2024
Comprehensive Review of Hereditary Ataxias and Optic Neuropathies, Neurology Clinics, 2023
